Change c0437. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. V; 1831 Ch. XXII.

Context before (unchanged): Sweet and beloved Elizabeth!

1818 text: I read and re-read her letter, and some softened feelings stole into my heart, and dared to whisper paradisaical dreams of love and joy; but the apple was already eaten, and the angel's arm bared to drive me from all hope.

1831 text: I read and re-read her letter, and some softened feelings stole into my heart, and dared to whisper paradisiacal dreams of love and joy; but the apple was already eaten, and the angel's arm bared to drive me from all hope.

Diff: I read and re-read her letter, and some softened feelings stole into my heart, and dared to whisper [-paradisaical-] {+paradisiacal+} dreams of love and joy; but the apple was already eaten, and the angel's arm bared to drive me from all hope.

Context after (unchanged): Yet I would die to make her happy.

result.rationale: "paradisaical" becomes "paradisiacal", a variant spelling of the same adjective with identical meaning. The surrounding Eden imagery (apple, angel's arm) is unchanged, so there is no interpretive effect.
